claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my child Alex, who's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'd like to ask you some questions about Alex to determine eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in any form of approved education or training?** (For example, A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQ Level 3 or below, or other approved courses)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is in sixth form doing A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. 

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I live in Leeds.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you.

**Do you live with Alex, or do they live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. They live elsewhere at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. This is an important factor for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Are you making any financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep?** (This could include things like money for food, clothes, pocket money, or contributing to their accommodation costs)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I contribute towards their living costs - things like clothes, food, and other expenses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep, and how often do you make these contributions?** (For example, weekly, monthly, or in lump sums)

This is important because to continue receiving Child Benefit when a child lives elsewhere, you generally need to contribute at least as much as the Child Benefit payment itself.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £30 a week towards Alex's upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful information.

**Has Alex started any paid work? And if so, how many hours per week do they work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work. They're focused on their studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 18 years old and in sixth form doing A-levels (approved education)
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives elsewhere (not with you)
- You contribute £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep
- Alex is not working

The key factor here is that Alex doesn't live with you. According to the rules, you can usually continue to get Child Benefit when your child lives with someone else if you make contributions to their upkeep that are at least equal to the Child Benefit payment amount.

**Do you know what the current Child Benefit weekly rate is, or would you be able to check if your £30 per week contribution meets or exceeds the Child Benefit amount you would receive for Alex?**

This is important because the rules state you need to contribute "at least the same amount as Child Benefit" to remain eligible when the child lives elsewhere.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure what the exact Child Benefit rate is at the moment. Is £30 a week enough?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand you're not certain about the current Child Benefit rates. Unfortunately, I don't have access to the specific current weekly rates within the information provided to me, so I cannot definitively confirm whether your £30 per week contribution meets the threshold requirement.

However, I can tell you that according to the rules, when a child lives with someone else, you can continue to receive Child Benefit if you contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards your child's upkeep.

**One more important question: Has anyone else claimed Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, the person Alex is currently living with)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Let me also ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Do you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000 per year?** (This wouldn't affect your eligibility, but you may need to pay a tax charge on the Child Benefit received)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: You didn't ask me about this earlier, but I should mention - Alex hasn't actually come to live with me yet. I'm in the process of adopting them, but they haven't moved in with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you very much for clarifying that - this is a very important detail that changes the situation significantly.

So to confirm my understanding:

**You are in the process of adopting Alex, who is 18 years old and doing A-levels, but Alex has not yet come to live with you. Is that correct?**

And a follow-up question: **Where is Alex currently living?** (For example, are they in care, living with foster carers, or in another arrangement?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct. Alex is 18, doing A-levels, and I'm adopting them but they haven't moved in with me yet. They're living in another arrangement at the moment, not with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification.

**Could you tell me more about Alex's current living arrangement? Specifically:**
- **Are they living with foster carers, in local authority care, or with friends/family?**
- **Is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance costs?**

This is important because the rules treat adoption and fostering situations differently, and whether the local council is contributing affects eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: They're not in foster care or local authority care. They're just living elsewhere while we work through the adoption process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Just to make sure I have the complete picture:

**Has Alex come to live with you at all yet during this adoption process, or are they still entirely living elsewhere while the adoption is being arranged?**

The reason I ask is that the rules state you can claim Child Benefit for a child you're adopting "as soon as any child you're adopting comes to live with you" - you don't have to wait until the adoption process is complete.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't come to live with me at all yet. They're still living elsewhere while we're going through the adoption process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. That's very important information.

Let me also confirm: **Are you currently the person legally responsible for Alex, or does someone else currently have parental responsibility while the adoption process is ongoing?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Someone else currently has parental responsibility while we're going through the adoption process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to make an assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarize the situation:
- Alex is 18 years old and in sixth form doing A-levels
- You are in the process of adopting Alex, but they haven't come to live with you yet
- Alex is living elsewhere, and someone else currently has parental responsibility
- You contribute £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep
- You live in the UK
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Based on the Child Benefit rules, the key issue here is that **you can claim Child Benefit for a child you're adopting as soon as they come to live with you** - you don't have to wait until the adoption is complete. However, Alex has not yet come to live with you.

Additionally, to qualify for Child Benefit, you normally need to be responsible for the child - either by living with them or by making contributions towards their upkeep. Since someone else currently has parental responsibility and Alex hasn't moved in with you yet, and given Alex's age (18), this presents complications regarding whether you would be considered "responsible" for Alex under the Child Benefit rules at this stage.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, **you are currently not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

The rules state that you can claim Child Benefit for a child you're adopting **as soon as they come to live with you** - you don't need to wait until the adoption process is complete. However, since Alex hasn't yet moved in with you and someone else currently has parental responsibility, you don't yet meet the requirement of being "responsible for the child" under Child Benefit rules.

**The good news is:** Once Alex does come to live with you as part of the adoption process, you would be able to claim Child Benefit at that point. You wouldn't need to wait for the adoption to be finalized - just for Alex to actually move in with you.

If you have any questions about this decision or would like clarification, please feel free to ask.
